extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, USPTO training staff, and external stakeholders (agents, attorneys, inventors, technical trainers) interested in patent examination training and quality programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program outline for developing and delivering USPTO training for patent examiners and external stakeholders, including topical legal training (35 U.S.C. sections), delivery formats, stakeholder courses (STEPP, PETTP, SEE), and recurring Patent Quality Chats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-driven training development
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO continues to develop training for both Examiners and External Stakeholders, based on data from MRF reviews, feedback from internal and external stakeholders, and customer perception surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training topics and priorities should be informed by MRF review data, stakeholder feedback, and customer perception surveys. (Link to USPTO Examination Guidance and Training Materials.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage for new and experienced examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner training is provided for both newly hired and experienced examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training may be tailored and delivered Corps-wide or to specific disciplines to meet different experience levels and technical areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple delivery styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Refresher legal training is developed and delivered via various styles: Lecture style; Interactive Computer Based Training (CBT); Workshops; Combinations thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select delivery methods (lecture, CBT, workshops, blended) appropriate to content complexity and audience needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility training (35 U.S.C. §101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed this fiscal year: 35 U.S.C. §101 CBT Subject Matter Eligibility on Abstract Ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted CBT to address abstract-idea analysis under §101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraphs and 112(f) training
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed this fiscal year: 35 U.S.C. §112(f) CBT introduction of new form paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce and demonstrate new form paragraphs for 112(f) via CBT; follow-up workshops may provide deeper, technology-specific examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(f) workshop with technology-specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: In-Progress: 35 U.S.C. §112(f) Workshop — follow-up to the CBT training earlier in the year; driven by technology-specific examples including instructions on how to use the new form paragraphs to establish claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops should use concrete technology examples to show how to apply form paragraphs to claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on novelty (35 U.S.C. §102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development for delivery later this fiscal year: 35 U.S.C. §102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop modules that clarify novelty analyses and application to claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on obviousness (35 U.S.C. §103) with focus on modification of references and reasons/motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development: 35 U.S.C. §103, Modification of References and Reasons/Motivation for Obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach methods for explaining modifications of references and articulating reasons/motivation in obviousness rejections and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description training emphasizing new matter (35 U.S.C. §112(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development: 35 U.S.C. §112(a) Written Description - The emphasis will be on new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus training on identifying new matter and ensuring claims/specification satisfy written description requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal analysis and persuasive writing for 103 responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development: Legal Analysis and Writing, 103 - Responding to Arguments and Persuasive Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instruction on constructing persuasive examiner responses and rebuttals in the context of obviousness analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention training
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development: Unity of Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover how to assess and handle unity/restriction issues during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s Answer practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development: Examiner’s Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train examiners on drafting Examiner’s Answers and procedural/ substantive considerations when preparing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting (statutory & non-statutory) training
rubrics_metrics.description: Under development: Double Patenting (Statutory and Non-statutory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance and tools for identifying and analyzing double patenting issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Chat program format and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics in this program provide information on procedural and legal topics relating to patent examination; webinar chats consist of a brief presentation and Question & Answer; monthly webinar which will focus on a particular quality topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monthly webinars to both disseminate information on specific quality topics and gather stakeholder input; include presentations plus Q&A interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Chat topical examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Past Quality Chats have covered Double Patenting: Tools for Identifying Conflicting Claims & Statutory Double Patenting; Evaluating Unexpected Results in 37 C.F.R. 1.132 Affidavits; AIA-FITF: 102(a)(2) and Exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select practical, exam-related topics that clarify procedural/ substantive issues and provide examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEPP: 3-day external stakeholder training objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder Training on Examination Practice and Procedure (STEPP): 3-Day training on examination practice and procedure for external stakeholders (Agent/Attorney course, Inventor course) to provide external stakeholders with a better understanding of how and why an examiner makes decisions while examining a patent application and to aid in compact prosecution by disclosing to external stakeholders how examiners are taught to use the MPEP to interpret an applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design STEPP to enhance stakeholders’ understanding of examiner reasoning, MPEP use, and prosecution efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEPP Day 1 — first-read examination and claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Day 1: Role of an examiner and the steps an examiner would take when reading an application for the first time; claim interpretation and 35 U.S.C. 101 and 112 are emphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize initial application review steps and core patentability/definiteness principles on Day 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEPP Day 2 — search planning and mapping prior art (102/103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Day 2: Use of information gathered during Day 1 to plan a search and conduct a search; mapping of prior art to claims using 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach practical search strategies and how to map prior art references to claim limitations for novelty and obviousness analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEPP Day 3 — office actions, restriction, and post-exam options
rubrics_metrics.description: Day 3: Writing of an office action; discussion of restriction practices; post-examination options such as the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) and the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover drafting/understanding office actions, restriction practice, and available post-examination routes for applicants and examiners to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual instructor-led (VILT) Hops courses and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: New for FY18 is a virtual instructor-led training (VILT) Hops courses — one or more topics related to examination practice and procedure. Upcoming topics include Claim Interpretation - Product by Process; Functional Language Workshop - Claim interpretation and Definiteness Under 35 U.S.C. §112(b); Inherency, 35 U.S.C. §102/103 Rejections, and Official Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use VILT to deliver focused topical modules; choose topics that address common interpretation and rejection issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP) participation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: PETTP: Opportunity for technologists, scientists, engineers, and other experts from industry and academia to voluntarily provide technical training and expertise to patent examiners in-person or virtually from their location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit subject-matter experts from industry/academia to supplement examiner technical knowledge; allow in-person or virtual delivery and list available satellite offices for in-person visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Experience Education (SEE) host and funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: SEE: Opportunity for commercial, industrial, and academic institutions, within the continental U.S., to voluntarily host patent examiner technical site visits; The USPTO funds all SEE travel costs for patent examiner visits to host organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit SEE hosts to institutions within the continental U.S.; USPTO covers examiner travel costs — use SEE to expose examiners to real-world technical contexts.
